title: Medicaid Cuts Target Disabled Americans: $900B Slashed, States Begin Re-Institutionalizing
description_short: Medicaid Cuts Target Disabled Americans: $900B Slashed, States Begin Re-Institutionalizing
description_medium: The reconciliation law signed July 4, 2025, is projected to reduce federal Medicaid spending by about $911 billion over ten years, according to the cited KFF analysis. That estimate concerns federal spending, not service losses for specific people. The analysis does not establish the entry’s claims about home-care cuts, reinstitutionalization or later Justice Department policy.
description_long: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4, 2025 cut a projected $900 billion-plus from Medicaid over a decade, and the June 2026 DOJ Olmstead opinion signaled the end of federal enforcement of community integration for people with disabilities. Iowa and other states began quietly reducing home health aide coverage and in-home support services that allow disabled people to avoid institutionalization. The Trump administration moved oversight of special education from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services under RFK Jr., whose public statements dismissing the severity of conditions like autism drew sharp rebukes from disability advocates. New Medicaid work requirements taking effect January 1, 2027 are expected to strip coverage from people with disabilities who cannot navigate complex exemption bureaucracies. Sen. Tammy Duckworth called the combination of cuts and DOJ opinion an attack on one of the most basic civil rights of Americans with disabilities.
organization_tags: Department of Health and Human Services

title: Maine Secretary of State Removes Trump from Ballot
description_short: Maine Secretary of State Removes Trump from Ballot
description_medium: On December 28, 2023, Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows became the first state official to unilaterally remove a presidential candidate from the ballot, ruling Trump disqualified under the 14th Amendment insurrection clause. Bellows cited Trump role in the January 6 Capitol attack in her decision. Trump appealed. The ruling was stayed pending Supreme Court review. Combined with the Colorado ruling, the decisions forced the Supreme Court to definitively address whether January 6 constituted insurrection.

title: Supreme Court agrees to hear immunity case - Jan 6 trial delayed (Apr 22, 2024)
description_short: SCOTUS agreed to hear Trump's immunity appeal, effectively pausing the Jack Smith Jan 6 federal trial until after the election — a massive delay benefiting Trump politically.
description_medium: On April 22, 2024, the Supreme Court agreed to hear Donald Trump’s appeal claiming presidential immunity from prosecution in the federal January 6 case. The supplied synopsis says the trial schedule was paused until after the 2024 election. The linked New York Times article covers Trump’s 2023 indictment, not the Court’s order or the resulting schedule.

title: Flood of Racist and Antisemitic Memes
description_short: Flood of Racist and Antisemitic Memes
description_medium: Throughout the fall of 2024, Donald Trump escalated his use of Truth Social to amplify racist, antisemitic, and white nationalist memes. He repeatedly 're-truthed' content from QAnon accounts and white supremacist users. This included AI-generated imagery and explicit dog whistles targeting minorities and political opponents, normalizing extreme fringe rhetoric in a mainstream presidential campaign.
